 Donald Trump and Joe Biden met in the Oval Office in November 2024
 Credit : AP/Evan Vucci
 Lily Shanagher
 Foreign Breaking News Reporter. 
 Harriet Barber
 Updated 
 10 November 2026 7:15pm GMT
 Published 
 10 November 2026 12:14pm GMT
 Donald Trump wrote Joe Biden a gracious letter on the day he left the White House despite spending the months prior falsely claiming Mr Biden had stolen the 2020 election .
 The handwritten note, left in the Oval Office on Jan 20, 2021, was addressed simply “To ‘46’”, a reference to Mr Biden becoming the 46th president of the United States.
 In it, Mr Trump reflected warmly on his time in office, saying working every day in the Oval Office was a “blessing beyond imagination”, and expressed confidence that Mr Biden would “be true to yourself and the American people”.
 The letter, whose contents have remained secret for almost six years, is reproduced in Mr Biden’s forthcoming memoir, according to an excerpt obtained by the New York Times.
 “Many presidents have come and gone who simply governed as Republicans or Democrats,” Mr Trump wrote. “Largely, they did not change history, they were just swept along in its relentless tide. This will not happen to you because I know how much you love the American people.”
 He also wrote: “I hope you take a moment every single day to take stock of where you are and the people who came before you, the titans who shaped the course of human events.”
 The letter was written on White House stationery with Mr Trump’s signature black Sharpie. He ended the note: “May God bless you and Jill, and may God bless America!”
 Mr Biden, in his book, said it was “as if there were two Donald Trumps”.
 He said his predecessor had “deeply destabilised our democracy” and had “not offered the traditional meeting between presidents”.
 “But here he was, offering his best wishes in warm language that sounded like it was coming from an old friend,” Mr Biden wrote.
 Mr Trump continues to falsely claim the 2020 election was rigged and has publicly blamed Mr Biden for various problems. On Tuesday, Steven Cheung, his communications director, echoed this message, saying: “Joe Biden should have heeded the president’s wise words, but instead he tried to destroy this country and weaponise the justice system against his political enemies. Biden is a disgrace, and America is better off with him no longer as president.”
 ‘If it weren’t for politics, we’d be good friends’
 According to the book, Mr Trump said to Mr Biden after his 2024 win: “You know, Joe, if it weren’t for politics, I believe we’d be good friends.”
 “Yes, if it weren’t for politics, we’d spend all our time golfing together.”
 Mr Biden said he was “too stunned to respond”.
 Mr Trump also told Mr Biden that he was relieved that he did not have to run against him , the former president claimed in his memoir.
 Mr Biden said Mr Trump had told him that ‘if it weren’t for politics, we’d spend all our time golfing together’
 Credit : AP/Chris Kleponis
 The former US president said Mr Trump made the claim when the two men sat down for an Oval Office meeting eight days after the 2024 election.
 Mr Biden had been forced to withdraw his candidacy late in the race to make way for Kamala Harris after mounting concerns over his age and health. It led to a resounding defeat for the Democrats after an acrimonious campaign.
 However, Mr Biden said that Mr Trump was “immediately chatty and surprised me by adopting a tone so friendly that I thought he might be putting me on.
 “It bordered on fawning,” he added.
 ‘He was buttering me up’
 Mr Trump also complimented his predecessor’s performance on job creation, calling it “extraordinary”.
 “I didn’t really understand why he was buttering me up, so I cut off his compliments to move on to the business at hand,” Mr Biden added.
 In his book, titled Promise Me, America, the former US president claims that when he tried to discuss issues he felt would dominate his presidency, Mr Trump was more interested in discussing the personalities of foreign leaders “as if we were sharing gossip about people at a dinner party”.
 Mr Biden, 83, writes that he was worried that his administration’s policies would be on the chopping block, with Mr Trump reversing many of his decisions from day one.
 He excoriates Mr Trump’s actions following that day, including leaving the Paris climate accord and pardoning nearly 1,600 people who marched on Capitol Hill on Jan 6, 2021, during the certification of the election result.
 Capitol riot was ‘insurrection’
 “It was clearly going to be a crueller government,” Mr Biden writes, pointing to attacks on democracy, people of colour and Democratic states.
 Of Jan 6, Mr Biden says Mr Trump “led an insurrection”.
 “His goal was to remain in power after the American people had voted him out of office,” he writes, adding that his actions “should never be forgotten” and should “follow him to his grave”.
 Mr Biden said that Donald Trump’s actions on Jan 6 2021 ‘should follow him to his grave’
 Credit : Reuters/Leah Millis
 “To this day, Trump and his supporters continue to preen and posture like they’re supporters of law enforcement,” he writes.
 “Here’s my view: You don’t get to turn a blind eye to cops being punched, speared, sprayed and brutalised and call yourself a friend of law enforcement.
 “What Trump did on January 6, 2021, should never be forgotten. It should follow him to his grave.”
 Mr Biden, who is being treated for cancer , withdrew from his battle with Mr Trump in 2024 after a flawed campaign in which his mental faculties were questioned and Democrats urged him to drop out for fear he would not win.
 Mr Trump and Mr Biden duellling in a televised debate
 Credit : Avalon
 His book comes out as Democrats have secured both the House and the Senate following the midterms in a sharp rebuke to the Trump administration and its policies.
 But Mr Biden’s own legacy remains complicated, with many Democrats critical of his support for Israel during its war in Gaza, US withdrawal from Afghanistan and his son Hunter’s legal troubles.
 Mr Biden’s book is set for release on Nov 17, although his promotion tour has been scaled back because of his ongoing cancer battle.
